text:
ops-bot: [ALERT] auth-proxy unusual request pattern (rate spike + 403s) from 34.201.22.0/24 detected by anomaly-detector. threshold breached: 6m avg 12x baseline. starting thread for triage
Eli (infra): got the page, I'm pulling the initial logs now. can someone confirm impact to customers?
Maya SRE: seeing a correlated uptick in auth failures and rejected tokens in edge logs. sample logs:```
[2026-06-07T14:02:12Z] proxy-1 auth - src=34.201.22.45 method=POST path=/v1/session status=403 token_id=svc-prod-abc123 reason=invalid_sig
[2026-06-07T14:02:14Z] proxy-2 auth - src=34.201.22.45 method=POST path=/v1/session status=401 token_id=svc-prod-abc123 reason=expired
```
Samir: that IP range is from a cloud-scrape ASN we haven't seen much from. could be credential stuffing or misconfigured mirror. check if any logs were forwarded to third-party indexers.
Eli (infra): confirmed some auth debug logs were recently archived to s3://redwood-debug-logs/ingest/ (s3 event at 2026-06-07T13:58). I'm worried about sensitive headers being included in those debug captures.
Security Oncall: paging in. immediate priorities: 1) contain (block offending sources at edge), 2) assess data exposure (which logs + keys), 3) rotate affected creds if needed, 4) notify legal/customer-facing if exposure confirmed.
Lina (prod-eng): rolling WAF rule now for 34.201.22.0/24 via cloudflare dashboard. applying 403 with challenge to buy time.
Maya SRE: applied ip block on proxy-ingress group in k8s-network-policy, confirmed drop at loadbalancer. traffic from that range down >95% in the last 90s.
Eli (infra): running quick grep across archived debug bucket for auth headers and tokens:```bash
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-debug-logs/ingest/ --recursive | grep 2026-06-07 | awk '{print $4}' | xargs -n1 aws s3 cp s3://redwood-debug-logs/ingest/{} - | jq -r '.headers.Authorization?'
```
ops-bot: scan task queued: s3-scan-job-20260607-001. ETA ~2m for initial report.
Samir: if debug captures contain full Authorization headers we need immediate key rotation for any exposed service tokens. which tokens are being logged by the auth service right now?
Eli (infra): looks like a handful of internal svc tokens were logged because of an old debug flag. tokens matched pattern svc-.*-alpha and svc-.*-prod. I've pulled sample file with masked tokens for now.
Security Oncall: escalate: assume compromise of any token present in those logs until proven otherwise. start rotation plan. Samir, can you coordinate service token rotation and publish a short blast to ops?
Samir: on it. rotating CI/deployment service tokens first (lowest blast radius): endpoint: POST /admin/rotate-token {service_id}. using `rotate-service-token --service=ci-runner` for the immediate run. will publish rotation list in #incidents when done.
Lina (prod-eng): heads up: rotating tokens may cause CI jobs to fail if they pull secrets from the old token. Samir, coordinate with CI owners to do a rolling swap and graceful retry logic.
Maya SRE: customer impact check: telemetry shows a small percentage (~0.7%) of production requests got 401 while we applied blocks/rotations. no widespread outages. impacted customers list being compiled via billing account mapping.
Security Oncall: start preservation: snapshot S3 bucket (versioning exists). create forensic copy to secure-logs account. keep original immutable. also open a JIRA security ticket and attach evidence.
Eli (infra): forensic copy kicked off:```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-debug-logs/ingest/ s3://secure-logs/forensics/20260607 --recursive --storage-class STANDARD_IA
```
legal-notify-bot: @legal-team: potential log exposure detected; please advise on notification timeline if PII or customer tokens found.
Legal (via bot): acknowledged. will join if PII confirmed; otherwise await security assessment.
ops-bot: s3-scan-job-20260607-001 completed: found 24 entries containing Authorization-like headers; 6 of those match patterns for long-lived service tokens. report saved to secure-logs/forensics/20260607/scan-report.json
Samir: rotating 6 affected service tokens now. commands:```bash
for svc in svc-prod-abc123 svc-prod-def456 svc-ci-789; do rotate-service-token --service=$svc && echo "$svc rotated"; done
```
Samir: rotation completed for the critical three, remaining three in progress (downstream owners were paged).
Maya SRE: I pushed a canary check to verify token revocation: hitting internal token-introspect with old token returns 401 now for rotated ones. good.
Lina (prod-eng): added short-term rate limits on auth endpoints per IP to reduce brute-force risk. config snippet:```yaml
auth:
  per_ip_rps: 5
  burst: 10
```
Security Oncall: prepare external comms: if we confirm any customer tokens exposed, we need a scoped notification. Ops/product, please draft a customer-facing note with impacted service list and remediation steps. keep it high level initially.
Eli (infra): also found one ElasticSearch forwarding rule that shipped debug logs to a staging index `staging-logs-20260607` in the analytics cluster. searching that index now for any tokens. if found, temp-stop replication and snapshot index.```curl
POST /staging-logs-20260607/_search
{ "query": { "match_phrase": { "headers.authorization": "svc-" } } }
```
ops-bot: elastic-scan job queued. ETA 3m.
Maya SRE: quick customer impact note: affected flows are token-intro, service-to-service auth for background tasks; user interactive sessions largely unaffected. will update if that changes.
Security Oncall: decision log: containment successful (edge block + rate-limit + token rotations). exposure likely limited to internal service tokens and some auth debug lines in a single s3 bucket and a staging index. severity: elevated (P2) until full index scan completes.
Samir: posting rotation summary in thread when all done. also creating short runbook to hard-disable debug capture flag in auth service and push a safety check to CI gating.
Lina (prod-eng): PR for removing debug capture flag: https://git.internal/redwood/auth-service/pull/312 - including test to ensure Authorization header is never logged.
Security Oncall: assign follow-ups: 1) full index & bucket scan (forensics) -> Security; 2) rotate any remaining exposed tokens -> Samir; 3) postmortem + timeline -> Maya; 4) customer comms draft -> Product/Support.
Eli (infra): handing off to Security Oncall for deeper investigation. I'll keep monitoring the edge for any resurgence.
Security Oncall: taking over. if anyone sees traffic spike again, @Security Oncall will re-open paging. adding retention of forensic artifacts and scheduling 1:30h deep dive room in 20m.
Maya SRE: thanks all — I'll produce initial incident timeline in the ticket and attach logs we pulled.
Samir: final rotation status: all 6 affected tokens rotated; 2 downstream owners notified and rotated, 4 rotated by infra, no cascading failures observed beyond brief CI job retries.
legal-notify-bot: legal acknowledged pending further info.
ops-bot: thread auto-summary: containment measures applied, tokens rotated, artifacts preserved. severity P2 -> monitoring.
Security Oncall: leaving a note: do not delete debug files until legal signs off on retention policy. will follow up with a full RCA and next steps.
Lina (prod-eng): closing my actions — WAF rule will stay for 48h unless cleared.
Eli (infra): last check at 2026-06-07T14:25Z showed auth error rate back to baseline. monitoring for 2h.
Maya SRE: last_message: creating postmortem draft and pinging CS for customer communication if needed.
